sentences.text: This dinosaur possesses unique physical characteristics not seen in other titanosaurs.
The neural spine of its vertebrae appears V-shaped from the side and resembles a Greek cross when viewed in cross-section.
Its cervical and dorsal vertebrae are opisthocoelous, while the caudal vertebrae are procoelous.
The vertebrae possess only a short crest on the posterior side of their spinous processes.
The ilium is pneumatized, meaning it is filled with internal air spaces.
Lohuecotitan was a relatively large sauropod measuring between 15 and 20 meters in length, though its neck length is unknown.
The semicircular canals are contracted and highly curved.
More than 10,000 fossils have been collected, including over twenty sets of partial titanosaur skeletons in anatomical connection.
The fossil locality was discovered in 2007 during the construction of the Madrid-Valencia high-speed railway.
Fossil remains were found at the Lo Hueco site in Fuentes, Cuenca, Spain.
The only known species in the genus is Lohuecotitan pandafilandi, which was described and named in 2016.
The species was named and described in 2016 by Verónica Díez Díaz, Pedro Mocho, Adrián Páramo, Fernando Escaso, Fátima Marcos Fernández, José Luis Sanz, and Francisco Ortega.
The genus name combines the type locality with the Greek word 'titan'.
The genus name references the fossil site name combined with the term 'titan,' alluding to the giants of Greek mythology.

The species name pandafilandi refers to the giant Pandafilando de la Fosca Vista, a character from Miguel de Cervantes Saavedra's novel Don Quixote, commemorating the 400th anniversary of the author in 2016.

The holotype consists of a partial skeleton lacking a skull, including three cervical vertebrae, six dorsal vertebrae, parts of sacral vertebrae, twenty caudal vertebrae, ribs, chevrons, a left ulna, both ischia, a left pubis, part of the right foot, and some indeterminate bones.
Lohuecotitan confirms that a rich radiation of titanosaurs occurred in the late Cretaceous in Europe, specifically on the ancient Iberian-Armorican island.
Lohuecotitan belongs to the class Saurischia.
The parent group of Lohuecotitan is Eutitanosauria.
The exact relationship of Lohuecotitan to other derived lithostrotians such as Opisthocoelicaudia, Alamosaurus, Trigonosaurus, Saltasaurinae, and Nemegtosauridae could not be determined.
It lived during the late Cretaceous, approximately 72 million years ago during the Maastrichtian, in what is now Europe.
Lohuecotitan lived during the Campanian to Maastrichtian time range, from 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
The fossil-bearing formation dates from the Upper Campanian to the Lower Maastrichtian and represented a muddy coastal floodplain.
